Subject: A cup of coffee needs 8.8 hours before bed; a pre-workout dose needs 13 (Gardiner 2023 systematic review)
Why: Gardiner et al. 2023 systematically reviewed caffeine dose and timing, finding the cutoff depends on dose and sleep outcome.
Citation: Gardiner C et al. (2023). The effect of caffeine on subsequent sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Sleep medicine reviews. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36870101/
Visual system: A single bedtime timeline holds a coffee cup and pre-workout scoop at their different cutoffs.
Hook option B: A pre-workout can outlast the workout
Hook option C: The caffeine cutoff changes with the dose
Slide 1:
Headline: Your coffee has a bedtime
Body: A coffee and a pre-workout do not get the same cutoff.
Slide 2:
Headline: Caffeine does not leave on your schedule
Body: The clock starts when you finish the drink.
Slide 3:
Headline: More caffeine needs more runway
Body: For a 107 mg coffee, the modeled window was 8.8 hours.
On-slide source: Gardiner et al., 2023
Slide 4:
Headline: Pre-workout is not just stronger coffee
Body: For a 217.5 mg pre-workout, it was 13.2 hours.
On-slide source: Gardiner et al., 2023
Slide 5:
Headline: Work backward from bedtime
Body: Use those windows as guides, then watch your own sleep.
Slide 6:
Headline: Dose and timing belong together
Body: The useful question is how much and how late.

Subject: A fixed wake time can matter more than forcing bedtime
Why: CBT-I guidelines and circadian research support stable wake timing while bedtime follows genuine sleepiness.
Citation: Edinger JD et al. (2021). Behavioral and psychological treatments for chronic insomnia disorder in adults: an American Academy of Sleep Medicine clinical practice guideline. Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33164742/
Visual system: The morning clock stays fixed while the bedtime clock stops being forced into place.
Hook option A: A better bedtime starts in the morning
Hook option C: Wake time may be the steadier lever
Slide 1:
Headline: A better bedtime starts in the morning
Body: Trying harder at night can make you more alert.
Slide 2:
Headline: Bedtime effort can increase arousal
Body: A forced bedtime is still time awake in bed.
Slide 3:
Headline: Wake time sets light, movement, and sleep-pressure timing
Body: Morning light and activity begin at wake-up.
Slide 4:
Headline: A stable morning makes bedtime more predictable
Body: A stable start makes the next night less random.
Slide 5:
Headline: Wake consistently and wait for sleepiness
Body: Keep wake time steady; go to bed when sleepy.
Slide 6:
Headline: Anchor the morning and let sleepiness lead
Body: The morning is easier to control than sleep onset.

Subject: A proprietary blend hides the dose you need to evaluate
Why: US labeling permits proprietary blends to list a total blend weight while withholding individual ingredient amounts.
Citation: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. 21 CFR § 101.36, Nutrition labeling of dietary supplements. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-101/subpart-C/section-101.36
Visual system: A real-looking supplement panel shows one blend total with individual doses visibly absent.
Hook option A: The ingredient list can hide the dose
Hook option B: A proprietary blend gives you one useful-looking number
Hook option C: Can you match this blend to a study?
Slide 1:
Headline: The ingredient list can hide the dose
Body: A long label can still leave the key question unanswered.
Slide 2:
Headline: The blend shows one combined weight
Body: The total weight covers every ingredient in the blend.
Slide 3:
Headline: Individual doses disappear inside it
Body: One ingredient could make up nearly all of that total.
Slide 4:
Headline: Without dose, research matching becomes impossible
Body: Without individual amounts, comparison with trials is guesswork.
Slide 5:
Headline: Look for every ingredient amount
Body: Look for a number beside each active ingredient.
Slide 6:
Headline: If the dose is hidden, the claim is hard to check
Body: Transparency is an ingredient-by-ingredient list.
